newsitem.title: UGANDA: Zairean refugees trickle into Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Zairean refugees trickle into Uganda.

text.p: At least 13,000 refugees, mostly Zaireans, have fled east Zaire into neighbouring Uganda and continue to arrive at the rate of 100 a day, a spokeswoman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said on Monday.
Wendy Rappaport told Reuters in Kampala that main entry points were in the southwestern and western districts but UNHCR had reports of refugees also crossing into Uganda from other centres.

"Some 13,000 refugees have entered Uganda since October 28. There are other people who have entered but not registered as refugees, others have been in transit to other places such as Europe," the UNHCR spokeswoman said. "They are Zaireans."
"They are still arriving at the rate of 100 per day."
She said the refugee agency, the International Federation of the Red Cross and Uganda Red Cross had provided food, water and sanitary facilities.
"The refugees are in good physical condition. We have had no trouble at all," she said.
Most refugees arrived at the border towns of Kisoro, Ishasha and Butogota and were being moved to other areas. Some refugees returned to Zaire, she said.
More than a million refugees have fled fighting in east Zaire. Most are Rwandan and Burundian Hutus who had lived in camps in the area since 1994 and most are missing.
Very few have gone home to Rwanda, but several thousand have been sent back to Burundi by the Zaire rebels.
Tanzania, already home to 600,000 earlier Hutu refugees, has taken in more than 20,000 Zaireans fleeing the fighting.
